title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 97
paragraphs: While they were doing this, the Delians too abandoned Delos and fled for refuge to Tenos. When the armament was sailing in, Datis went on ahead and did not let the ships anchor off the island of Delos itself, but had them moor at Rheneia across the strait. Then, having found out by inquiry where the Delians had gone, he sent a herald to address them with this message: “Holy men, why have you fled, thinking of me what is not fitting? I myself have at least this much sense, and beyond that I have been commanded by the king to do no harm to the land in which the two deities were born — neither to the land nor to its inhabitants. Return, therefore, to your own homes and dwell once more on your island.” Thus he proclaimed to the Delians by herald, and he then piled up on the altar three hundred talents' weight of frankincense and burned it.
